newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bakrie says no deal on Indocopper stake.
newsitem.headline: Bakrie says no deal on Indocopper stake.

text.p: Indonesia's conglomerate PT Bakrie & Brothers said on Thursday it is not negotiating with other parties to sell its stake in PT Indocopper Investama.
Bakrie has a 49-percent stake in Indocopper which has a 9.36-percent stake in PT Freeport Indonesia.
Freeport Indonesia, 81.28-percent owned by U.S. Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc, operates one of the world's largest copper and gold mines in Irian Jaya province.
"There is no negotiation and there is no deal as far as I'm aware," investor relations manager Suresh Kumar told Reuters.
Kumar also denied market talk that either timber baron Muhamad "Bob" Hasan or the government was in negotiations with the firm regarding the possible sale of its Indocopper stake.

Local newspapers reported on Thursday that Bakrie's chairman Aburizal Bakrie had denied Tuesday's comments to several reporters by Bakrie's senior vice president Nalin Rathod that the firm was negotiating to sell its Indocopper stake.
